transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vekulman.
The national hurricane says a tropical system
in the Gulf of Mexico is now turned into Hurricane Isaias.
Top winds are now at 80 miles per hour.
It could make landfall tomorrow night
on the Alabama Gulf Coast.
Lauren Lineham is with the Environmental Station Report,
WBHM.
It's been a pretty quiet hurricane season so far
with El Nino in place.
So areas from the Mississippi Gulf Coast
all the way to the Florida Panhandle,
especially along the coast,
have been stocking up on those hurricane supplies.
They know that hurricane plan.
And so for folks who are staying,
who have not had evacuation orders,
they are definitely making those preps
right along the coast.
But it's also the inland communities.
Lauren Lineham reporting.
Florida and Alabama have declared states of emergency.
A weakened storm system could race north
toward Tennessee and western Kentucky
after making landfall.
President Trump says he is turning part
of a private golf club that he owns in Florida
into a presidential-style retreat like Camp David.
Trump cited security as one of the reasons.
NPR's Emily Fang reports it's similar to his justification
for major architectural changes in Washington, D.C.
Representatives from the West Palm Beach Golf Club
have already submitted plans for the proposed retreat.
Future presidents, according to these plans,
would be given complimentary membership.
Trump says the golf club would be safer.
You don't have high buildings looming over it.
There's no high building looming over it,
which is no good either.
And they can get maximum safety.
It's a very, it's a very, it's a great idea.
He's also touted safety as one of the primary reasons
for building the East Wing Ballroom at the White House
and building a massive new triumphal arch in Washington.
Emily Fang, NPR News, the White House.
Houthi rebel forces in Yemen have claimed responsibility
for missile attacks on two Saudi airports this week.
Saudi Arabian authorities say three people have been killed
and more than 30 others wounded in those attacks.
NPR's Aya Batrawi has more.
Saudi Arabia says a Sudanese national was killed
and eight people wounded, some critically,
in an attack on the capital of Riyadh's international airport.
Another attack on an airport in Epa in the south
killed two women, one from Morocco,
the other from Algeria, and wounded 28 others.
Saudi Arabia provided no further details on the attacks
but said they occurred Tuesday and Wednesday.
The Houthis in Yemen, who are backed by Iran,
say they struck the airports with ballistic missiles.
They also warned international airlines
of the "consequences of continuing to operate flights
within Saudi airspace," calling it a theater for military
operations.
The attacks come as Saudi Arabia's Air Force and the allied
Yemeni government forces try to recapture Yemeni territory
along a Red Sea shipping route seized
by the Houthis last month.
Aya Batrawi, NPR News, Dubai.
You're listening to NPR.
The Swedish Academy has announced
that this year's Nobel Prize in Literature
has been awarded to Canadian author Anne Carson.
She is a poet, essayist, and professor of classics.
In honoring Carson with the Nobel Prize,
the Academy noted her playful dialogue
with the classical tradition.
It said that Carson has created new forms
for contemporary literature.
The federal agency tasked with regulating cryptocurrency
has been shrinking as prediction markets expand
and become more popular.
NPR's Lou Garrett reports the Commodity Futures Trading
Commission is now facing a federal investigation.
Last year, the CFTC saw a 20% workforce reduction
and a nearly 80% drop in fraud enforcement cases.
Jeff Laric, a former CFTC enforcement lawyer,
says these cuts weren't a coincidence.
He says the agency reduced staffing and crypto enforcement
soon after Trump won the 2024 election.
In order to show results to that industry,
some people were punished for bringing those cases.
There's now a federal probe into staffing levels
at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission
following a request from Massachusetts Senator
Elizabeth Warren.
In a statement to NPR, the CFTC says
it hopes to add 100 new employees in 2026.
Lou Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
The Arizona State Supreme Court says Saboteurs
got into its computer system last month
and stole personal information
on more than one million people.
This apparently happened when a court employee
clicked a malicious link in an email.
The high court says it has notified affected people.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Tropical system in Gulf of Mexico becomes Hurricane Isaias with 80 mph winds, expected landfall tomorrow on Alabama coast
Florida and Alabama declare states of emergency as weakened storm system could race north toward Tennessee and western Kentucky
President Trump plans to convert private Florida golf club into presidential retreat similar to Camp David, citing security concerns
Houthi rebels claim responsibility for missile attacks on two Saudi airports, killing three people and wounding over 30 others
Swedish Academy awards Nobel Prize in Literature to Canadian author Anne Carson for her work with classical tradition
Commodity Futures Trading Commission faces federal investigation after 20% workforce reduction and 80% drop in fraud enforcement cases
Arizona State Supreme Court reports computer breach exposed personal information of more than one million people
